title: Coherence-driven origin of metamagnetism in anisotropic heavy-fermion systems
authors: Ewan Scott, Zheyu Wu, Theodore I. Weinberger, Alexander G. Eaton, Michal P. Kwasigroch
abstract: A number of heavy-fermion materials exhibit magnetic field-induced metamagnetism: on applying a field along the magnetic hard axis, the magnetization first rises gradually, then jumps abruptly once a critical field is reached. Despite decades of phenomenological modeling, the microscopic origin of the pronounced magnetic anisotropy underlying this behavior has remained unresolved. The same is true of a related, long-standing puzzle: an anomalous maximum in the hard-axis susceptibility versus temperature. Both are complicated in $5f$ compounds by the dual localized-itinerant character of the relevant electrons. Here we develop an analytic $c$--$f$ theory of magnetic anisotropy in heavy-fermion metamagnets, identifying the mixed susceptibility $χ_{\rm cf}(T,h,p)$ as a single thermodynamic observable that unifies the anisotropic response across temperature, field, and pressure. We test this theory against primary and literature data for the heavy-fermion superconductor UTe$_2$, finding excellent quantitative agreement in the temperature, field, and pressure evolution of its magnetic anisotropy -- including a Kondo-coherence origin for the anomalous hard-axis susceptibility maximum, which we show is directly connected to the metamagnetic transition itself. Our results establish a general, microscopic, coherence-driven framework for anisotropic metamagnetism, applicable across the broad class of heavy-fermion compounds that display this phenomenology.
summary: This work presents a comprehensive analytic theory for magnetic anisotropy in heavy-fermion metamagnets. By introducing the mixed susceptibility $\chi_{cf}$, the authors successfully unify the understanding of field-induced metamagnetism and anomalous temperature dependencies across multiple thermodynamic variables. This framework establishes a general, microscopic model applicable to a broad class of correlated materials.
main_problem: The microscopic origin of pronounced magnetic anisotropy underlying metamagnetism and an anomalous maximum in hard-axis susceptibility in heavy-fermion materials remains unresolved.
main_result: The authors develop a general, coherence-driven framework using the mixed susceptibility $\chi_{cf}(T, h, p)$ that successfully unifies the anisotropic response across temperature, field, and pressure for these systems.
method: Development of an analytic $c$-$f$ theory based on extending the 2-fluid model to explicitly treat magnetic anisotropy arising from localized-itinerant electron interactions.
model_or_system: The study focuses on heavy-fermion compounds, particularly $	ext{UTe}_2$, modeling the system with two types of $f$-electrons: an itinerant ($f_1$) and a localized ($f_2$). The theory incorporates Kondo coupling and anisotropy interactions between these moments.
key_observables: Mixed susceptibility ($\chi_{cf}(T, h, p)$), critical magnetic field for metamagnetism ($h_m$), and the temperature of the susceptibility maximum ($T_{\max}$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), Magnetic Field ($h$), Pressure ($p$), Kondo coupling constants ($J_1, J_2$), and anisotropy parameters ($D_\eta$).
main_assumptions: The theory builds upon the 2-fluid model (Nakatsuji, Pines, Fisk) and utilizes mean-field approximations in the large-$N$ limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how $\chi_{cf}$ unifies anisotropic response across T, h, p; they also show theoretical predictions for $h_m(	heta_{bc})$ and $T_{\max}(	heta_{bc})$ compared to experimental data.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the unresolved puzzle of anisotropy in heavy-fermion metamagnets. It then develops the analytic $c$-$f$ theory centered on $\chi_{cf}$. Finally, it tests this theory against detailed measurements from $	ext{UTe}_2$, demonstrating its predictive power for both the susceptibility maximum and the metamagnetic transition.
why_interesting: The explicit derivation of a single thermodynamic observable ($\chi_{cf}$) that governs multiple complex phenomena (metamagnetism, susceptibility anomalies) provides a powerful, unified theoretical tool applicable to strongly correlated electron physics.
